sourceContinuation.policy: All declared outputs, including unchanged bytes, are source-produced and excluded from external and ABI patches.

limits: The explicit selected source producer runs before any external patch. Every owned byte is checked against the next entry and protected from patching; other native producers remain supplied inputs.
Source physics output is carried; only observed native after-to-next-before byte changes and declared caller ABI refreshes are supplied.
External patches may include native post-physics, AI, input, rendering or service producers; their individual authorship is not established by byte differences.
Next entry registers are native caller inputs. Stack refresh regions are explicit and are reported separately from semantic equality.

Bindings and aliases are rebuilt from carried source bytes each frame; module/thread/root descriptors and the full initial observation footprint remain stable. Under strict policy region metadata and resolved roots also remain identical.

The initial-observation policy admits no surplus bytes. Its fixed footprint is an observation window, not a logical-allocation capacity or entire-process-heap claim; newly reached memory outside it fails.
Resolved pointer roots may be mutable free-list heads; every observed value is reported rather than treated as a fixed allocation base.
Exact declared semantic spans and native returns are compared each frame, before any external overwrite. This does not establish a closed reconstructed game or wall-clock cadence.
